ops.title: A dict tool_response killed three cc-notes hook handlers on both fleet hosts
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-31 while diagnosing a `UserPromptSubmit` hook timeout on forge-studio. **Fixed on cc-notes main in `1b3b34d`**, unreleased — the deployed plugin cache (0.51.2) still carries the bug until a release is cut.

## The defect

`plugin/capt-hook/hooks/record.py:1067` and, verbatim, `plugin/capt-hook/hooks/compact.py:108`:

    def _tool_output(evt: BaseHookEvent) -> str:
        return getattr(evt, "tool_response", None) or ""

The annotation says `str`; Claude Code sends `tool_response` as a **dict** for structured tools. Every caller feeds the result to a regex, so the handler raised

    TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'dict'

at `record.py:1325` (`VERDICT_LANGUAGE_RE.search(_tool_output(evt))`) and the sibling call sites.

## Blast radius, measured

On this workstation, `~/.cache/captain-hook/logs`: **13 occurrences** across three handlers — `nudge_multiagent_synthesis` (11), `nudge_ci_triage_investigation` (2), `announce_pr_status` (1). Two more on forge-studio. **A dying handler takes its worker with it**, so the next dispatch for that project root pays a cold start — which is how this surfaced.

## The fix

One `common.tool_output` renders a non-string response as JSON (`json.dumps(..., default=str)`) and leaves absent, empty, and string responses exactly as before. Both duplicated copies are deleted in favour of it, so the bug cannot exist twice again. `_minted_id` benefits: it parses `{"id":"..."}` out of the text, which a JSON-rendered dict now actually provides.

Bracketed: the dict case fails against the old body and passes against the new one; full helper suite green (`uv run plugin/capt-hook/hooks/tests/test_cc_notes.py`).

## Not the cause of the reported timeout

The `UserPromptSubmit hook timed out after 10s` on forge-studio is a **different** thing: that host's only `UserPromptSubmit` entry in `~/.claude/settings.json` is Orca's (`~/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh`) with `timeout: 10`, and the box was at load average 13.76 with 21 sessions. capt-hook's own hooks come from the plugin with `timeout: None`. Worker dispatch there measured 0.60-2.01s warm.</body>

ops.text: cc-notes cuts a release containing 1b3b34d so the deployed plugin cache stops raising the TypeError
After that release, `grep -h 'TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object' ~/.cache/captain-hook/logs/*.log` stops growing on both hosts
